name: Amertech Engineering, Inc.
what_they_do: Civil and environmental engineering, planning and surveying firm doing land planning, site engineering, subdivision/roadway/grading and stormwater design, sanitary and water systems, permits and expert testimony. Also serves as municipal engineer for several central New Jersey towns.
customers: Private developers and landowners plus municipal governments, boards of education and utility authorities.

size_signals.signal: States the firm and its predecessors have provided engineering services in New Jersey for over 80 years

Lists long-running municipal appointments: Monroe Township (35 years), Plainsboro (19 years), Cranbury (10 years), Clark (over 10 years), plus South Brunswick, East Brunswick, Franklin, New Brunswick, Highland Park and Edison
Separate Client Profile and Project Profile pages

listing.reviews: No review count shown on the Maps panel

website_review.primary_cta: No button or quote CTA; only a 'Contact Us' page link
website_review.online_booking_or_quote: Legacy table-based form (first/last name, email, company, mailing address, product/service, contact method); no quote or booking flow
website_review.trust_signals: 80-year history, long municipal client list, project profile page; no photos of work, no testimonials, no licences stated
website_review.out_of_date_signs: Copyright reads '© 2011 – 2016'; no viewport meta tag so the phone view is a shrunken desktop layout; header email link points to a placeholder 'ourname@ouraddress.com'; 'Ridgewod Avenue' typo in the header address; page filenames are id1.html/id4.html/id61.html
website_review.search_basics: Title is the company name only; no meta description; no town or service keywords; services exist only as body text on a few legacy pages
top_issues: Site is about a decade out of date (2016 copyright) and not mobile-responsive — the 390px view renders as an unreadable shrunken desktop page
The email link in the site header is a broken placeholder (ourname@ouraddress.com)
Google listing is unclaimed with a 3.4 rating, no hours and no photos
No meta description, no JSON-LD, no tel: links, no viewport tag

agent_readiness.notes: Google Maps shows 'Claim this business' and 'Add hours' — unclaimed and incomplete. robots.txt is an empty file, so nothing is blocked. Zero JSON-LD. Services are readable text but sit in legacy table markup; no hours, no service-area statement, no price ranges. The contact form is a 2000s-era table form with unlabelled fields an agent cannot reliably map, and the header email link is broken.

operations_signals.signal: Contact page invites phone, fax or a legacy web form with no acknowledgement or ticketing path (inference: enquiries handled manually by office staff)
Municipal engineering appointments across roughly ten towns imply a heavy, recurring agenda and report workload (inference from the client list)

top_opportunities.opportunity: Rebuild the site responsive-first around services and towns served, with a working contact/quote form, click-to-call and a fixed email link
top_opportunities.evidence: 2016 copyright, no viewport meta (broken phone layout), placeholder mailto in the header, id-numbered page filenames

top_opportunities.opportunity: Claim and complete the Google Business Profile with hours, categories, services and project photos to lift visibility around a 3.4 rating
top_opportunities.evidence: Maps panel shows 'Claim this business', 'Add hours', no photos, rating 3.4

top_opportunities.opportunity: Project-intake agent that captures parcel, municipality, project type and deadline from developer enquiries and drafts the first response
top_opportunities.evidence: Intake is a legacy form plus phone/fax; the site markets feasibility studies, zoning analysis and permits where scoping questions are predictable

scores.reasons: Gap: ten-year-old non-responsive site, broken email link, unclaimed low-rated listing, no schema or meta. Ability: 80-year-old firm with long municipal contracts and high project values. Ease: full rebuild is a project, though quick wins exist. Evidence: pages, mobile rendering and Maps panel inspected.
